sentence: Montelukast is a prescription medicine that helps keep airways from narrowing and helps prevent asthma attacks.
It is usually an add-on to other asthma medicines, and it is not a steroid.
Montelukast and zafirlukast block cysteinyl leukotriene type 1 receptors but not type 2 receptors.
Leukotrienes drive airway narrowing, leaky blood vessels, recruitment of eosinophils and long-term inflammation.
The MHRA warns that montelukast can cause neuropsychiatric reactions such as sleep disorders, hallucinations, anxiety, depression and changes in behaviour and mood.
The MHRA advises patients to speak to their prescriber immediately, or seek urgent medical attention, if these reactions occur.
Some epilepsy medicines, rifampicin and gemfibrozil may affect how montelukast works.
